speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with blisters on your forearm and ulcers on your mucosal surfaces; to help me narrow down the cause, have you noticed if these lesions are painful, and do you have a history of similar outbreaks or autoimmune conditions?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pemphigus Vulgaris. The combination of painful oral/mucosal ulcers, dermatomal-appearing blisters on the forearm, and a history of autoimmune disease (Graves') strongly points to an autoimmune blistering disorder. The recent start of captopril could also suggest drug-induced pemphigus, but the clinical picture fits Pemphigus Vulgaris best.
